scenes.headline: That parking QR code may be a sticker
scenes.body: A fake one, stuck over the real sign
scenes.say: Drivers, that parking QR code may be a fake sticker.

scenes.headline: A fake page takes your card
scenes.body: Card number, expiry date and security code.
scenes.say: Scammers stick their own QR code on parking meters. It opens a fake payment page that asks for your card number, expiry date and security code.

scenes.headline: Germany, Luxembourg, New Zealand
scenes.body: All warned drivers about fake parking QR codes this year.
scenes.say: This year, drivers were warned about fake parking QR codes in Germany, Luxembourg and New Zealand.

scenes.headline: AT does not use QR codes on any of our parking meters or machines.
scenes.say: In September, Auckland Transport said: AT does not use QR codes on any of our parking meters or machines.

scenes.headline: A QR code hides the web address.
scenes.body: Check where it really goes before you type anything.
scenes.say: Analyst note: a QR code hides the web address, so check where it really goes before you type anything.

scenes.headline: Do this tonight
items: Use the official app or the machine
Card entered? Call your bank now
scenes.say: Tonight: look for a sticker on top, use the official parking app or pay at the machine, and if you typed your card into a strange site, call your bank right away.
